prompt: A student tries to prove that a-run/b-run strings with equal counts are non-regular. They choose pumping length 4, choose `aaaabbbb`, pick the pumped piece as `aa`, double it and observe unequal counts. Which are genuine flaws? Select all that apply.

options.text: Fixing the pumping length at 4 rather than keeping it arbitrary
options.explanation: Flaw. The adversary chooses p. The proof must work for any p, so use p a’s followed by p b’s as the witness.

options.text: Choosing a specific y instead of handling every legal split
options.explanation: Flaw. The adversary chooses the split. Showing one bad split proves nothing.

options.text: Using two copies rather than zero copies
options.explanation: Not a flaw. Any single i that breaks membership is enough, and two copies works here.

options.text: Choosing a member of L at least as long as the pumping length
options.explanation: Not a flaw. This is required: s must be in L and at least p long.

workedExample: The proof must work for any proposed pumping length, not just four. It must also defeat every legal split, not merely the chosen aa. Choose a run of a characters as long as the proposed pumping length, followed by the same number of b characters. Every permitted pumped piece lies inside the first run; doubling any such non-empty piece makes the counts unequal. Either deletion or duplication can supply the contradiction here.
